description.value: The study investigated socio-emotional cognition and its neural correlates in behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia, semantic dementia, Alzheimer’s disease, and healthy controls using the Socio-Emotional Questionnaire and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: The current study had three major aims: (i) to tease apart the different dimensions of socio-emotional cognition, and determine how these different dimensions are affected in bvFTD, SD and AD; (ii) to investigate insight into socio-emotional cognition in bvFTD, SD and AD and; (iii) to identify the neural correlates subserving the different dimensions of socio-emotional cognition using voxel-based morphometry.

value: different dimensions of socio-emotional cognition would be affected in each patient group, with bvFTD and SD patients showing greater deficits across all dimensions of the SEQ compared to AD and controls
insight into socio-emotional deficits would be reduced in bvFTD, compared to both AD and controls
integrity of the frontal and temporal regions would underlie socio-emotional functioning

spans.text: It was hypothesized that: (i) different dimensions of socio-emotional cognition would be affected in each patient group, with bvFTD and SD patients showing greater deficits across all dimensions of the SEQ compared to AD and controls; (ii) insight into socio-emotional deficits would be reduced in bvFTD, compared to both AD and controls.
